Change scores are also reported (fluoxetine -21.45±12.20 vs placebo -15.30±11.70, P=0.076) but the end-of-treatment values were used per the plan. No M_diff computed because this is a three-arm trial analysed by ANOVA/ANCOVA. Report_ID: Self-rated overall premenstrual symptom severity (DRSP mean luteal-follicular symptom difference), fluoxetine vs placebo
Title: A Pilot Study to Compare Fluoxetine, Calcium, and Placebo in the Treatment of Premenstrual Syndrome
Author: Yonkers, Pearlstein, Gotman
Comment: No end-of-treatment means/SDs per arm are reported for the DRSP; only the mixed-model estimated group difference (B = -0.28) with 95% CI and a Cohen d are given. SE_diff = (-0.04 - (-0.53))/3.92 = 0.125, derived from the reported 95% CI (SE of the coefficient was not reported). Baseline DRSP means (SD) are available (fluoxetine 2.16 [0.86], placebo 1.29 [0.60]) but are BASELINE, not endpoint, so were not entered as group means. Reported Cohen d = 2.08 was computed non-standardly (between-group difference in change from visit 1 to visit 5 divided by the placebo group's SD at visit 5, not a pooled SD) and the fluoxetine arm had substantially higher baseline DRSP severity, so this d is likely inflated and not directly comparable to a conventional Hedges' g. Negative B favours fluoxetine. Abstract misquotes the DRSP CI as "-1.70 to -0.35" (that is the CGI-I CI); Table 2 value used.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Fluoxetine 10 mg twice daily (continuous daily dosing, 4 cycles)') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)

Participant type: Women aged 18-48 years with moderate to severe premenstrual syndrome (>=3 DSM-IV premenstrual symptoms with functional impairment, prospectively confirmed on daily ratings)
Recruitment source: On-site screening in private gynecologic practices plus community advertisements/posters, Providence RI and New Haven CT, 2001-2009
